meta.label: TVs
meta.attribution: Compares 20 specific 55-inch smart TV models, the most common living-room size, so that energy figures line up: 18 registered for sale in the EU (several also sold in the UK) and two US-only sets from Vizio, owned by Walmart since December 2024, and Roku. Energy comes from each model's EU Product Information Sheet in the European Product Registry for Energy Labelling (EPREL), under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2013. The score is the standard dynamic range (SDR) energy class, which already allows for screen size: A scores 100, B 88, C 76, D 64, E 52, F 40 and G 28. The on-mode power in watts, which is also the kWh used per 1,000 hours, and the high dynamic range class are in each note. The two US sets have no EU label. The US Department of Energy publishes on-mode power for them, but its test gives very different figures for the same sets (an LG C5 measures 77 W in the EU and 133 W in the US), so those figures are described rather than scored. The ENERGY STAR television list (data.energystar.gov) was checked and covers none of the US sets here. Durability is France's mandatory durability index (indice de durabilite) for televisions, in force since January 2025. It folds a repairability mark and a reliability mark into one score out of 10, which is multiplied by ten here. It is taken from the filings makers publish on data.gouv.fr, the French government's open data platform, matched to the exact EU registration, with any naming difference stated in the note. TCL, TP Vision (Philips) and Amazon have no filing there and the US sets are not sold in France, so durability is shown for 13 of 20 models. Software support is scored at ten points per year of operating-system or security updates the maker publicly promises, plus ten where the EU minimum applies, up to 90. That minimum, stated on every EU sheet, is 8 years of firmware availability and 7 or 8 years of spare parts after a model leaves the market. An EU-registered set with no published promise scores 40 and a US set with none scores 20. Promises worded 'up to' are taken at face value and flagged in the note. Privacy is about automatic content recognition (ACR), which identifies what is on screen in order to target ads, and other viewing-data collection. It starts from 50 for a platform that collects viewing data for advertising with the owner's consent. Collection that is on until the owner opts out lowers the score, as does a regulator's lawsuit or order, less where a settlement has since tightened consent. A platform that ships with ACR switched off raises it. Sources are the Texas Attorney General's December 2025 lawsuits against Samsung, LG, Sony, Hisense and TCL and the Samsung and LG settlements that followed, the FTC's 2017 Vizio case (history), Michigan's 2025 lawsuit against Roku, and each platform's own privacy policy or help page. Lawsuits are allegations, not findings. In the EU and UK, data protection law requires consent before viewing data is collected. Price is not scored because most makers do not sell directly, and retail TV prices change week to week. Picture quality is not scored. Sources: EPREL, data.gouv.fr, US DOE certification database, Texas Attorney General, FTC, Michigan Attorney General, maker privacy and product pages, Titan OS, Amazon help, BGR's August 2026 software support survey, Expert Reviews. Reviewed 2026-10. Suggest changes via Contribute.

products.name: Samsung U8000F 55-inch (TU55U8005FU)
products.description: Samsung's entry-level 4K Crystal UHD set for 2025. It sits in energy class G, the bottom of the EU scale, but comes with Samsung's longest software promise.

environment.note: Samsung TU55U8005FU's EU Product Information Sheet (EPREL 2205236) gives energy efficiency class G in standard dynamic range, with an on-mode power demand of 79 W, which is 79 kWh per 1,000 hours of viewing, on a visible screen area of 82.3 square decimetres; in high dynamic range it is class G at 118 W.

durability.note: France's durability index filing on data.gouv.fr lists Samsung model TU55U8005FUXXC, the France-market code for the same U8000F registration in the EU energy label database (TU55U8005FU), with a durability index of 7.5 out of 10, made up of a repairability mark of 6.47 and a reliability mark of 8.59, calculated on 2025-04-07.

longevity.note: For the U8000F, Samsung's Tizen developer site says, in a March 2025 post, 'Samsung’s smart TVs and appliances now receive OS upgrades for up to 7 years', covering feature and security updates. The EU Product Information Sheet adds a minimum 8 years of firmware availability and 7 years of spare parts after the model leaves the market. Scored at ten points per stated year of upgrades, plus ten for the EU minimum on top.

privacy.note: This U8000F runs Samsung Tizen software. Texas sued Samsung in December 2025 over automated content recognition (ACR), the feature that identifies what is on screen to target ads. In February 2026 the Texas Attorney General announced an agreement under which 'Samsung must halt any collection or processing of ACR viewing data without obtaining Texas consumers’ express consent' and must add clearer consent screens. Samsung TVs still use ACR for anyone who accepts it at setup; in the EU that consent is required by data protection law before collection.

longevity.note: Sony K-55XR8M2's EU Product Information Sheet (EPREL 2152088) states a minimum guaranteed availability of software and firmware updates of 8 years and of spare parts of 7 years, both counted from the end of placement on the market, and a supplier guarantee of 2 years. No fixed period of operating-system upgrades for this model was found, so the score reflects the EU minimum only.

products.name: Amazon Fire TV 4-Series 55-inch (4K55N402)
products.description: Amazon's own-brand 4K TV, registered in the EU energy label database under the Ember 4-Series name. Class G at 80 W, with a dated security-update guarantee. Amazon files no French durability index.

environment.note: Amazon 4K55N402U's EU Product Information Sheet (EPREL 2462779) gives energy efficiency class G in standard dynamic range, with an on-mode power demand of 80 W, which is 80 kWh per 1,000 hours of viewing, on a visible screen area of 82.3 square decimetres; in high dynamic range it is class G at 88 W.

longevity.note: BGR's August 2026 survey of smart TV software support reports that Amazon's 2025 Fire TV 2-Series, 4-Series and Omni lines are guaranteed security updates until 31 December 2030, a little over five years from launch, and that a set bought directly from Amazon gets at least four years from purchase if that runs later. These are security updates, not promised feature upgrades. The EU Product Information Sheet adds 8 years of firmware availability and 7 years of spare parts after the model leaves the market. Scored at ten points per year of guaranteed updates, plus ten for the EU minimum on top.

privacy.note: The Amazon 4-Series runs Amazon's Fire TV software. Amazon's own help page for Fire TV televisions says 'Amazon software collects information relating to your use of broadcast (terrestrial, satellite or cable) TV content' through the aerial and cable inputs, including channel and programme names, and that owners can opt out in the privacy settings, which makes collection the default. No regulator action over Fire TV viewing data was found.

products.name: Vizio Quantum 4K QLED 55-inch (VQD55R)
products.description: A low-cost US QLED from Vizio, owned by Walmart since December 2024. It is not sold in the EU, so it has no EU energy label; the US Department of Energy database lists 91.7 W in on mode and 216 kWh a year under the US test, which is not comparable with the EU figures and is not scored.

longevity.note: BGR's August 2026 survey of smart TV software support says it chose 'manufacturers that publicly state a concrete support period' and found four: Amazon, LG, Samsung and Hisense. Vizio is not among them, and no update period was found on its own pages. In the US there is no legal minimum period for firmware or spare parts like the EU's, so the score is lower than for EU-registered sets with no promise.

privacy.note: Vizio's privacy policy, updated in March 2026 to reflect Walmart's purchase of the company, says owners have a choice whether to provide Walmart with access to Viewing Data and other VIZIO OS data, and that Viewing Data can be turned off in the TV's Privacy & Legal settings. Walmart said when it completed the purchase in December 2024 that Vizio's operating system would help grow Walmart Connect, its advertising business. Vizio settled charges from the FTC and New Jersey in February 2017 that it had collected viewing histories from about 11 million TVs without consent; the order required it to get express consent.

products.name: Roku Select Series 4K 55-inch
products.description: A budget 4K QLED TV designed and sold by Roku in the US, and the US budget floor in this list. It is not sold in the EU, so no EU energy label exists and energy is not scored; Roku's own US models are certified with the US Department of Energy under a different test.

longevity.note: BGR's August 2026 survey of smart TV software support says it chose 'manufacturers that publicly state a concrete support period' and found four: Amazon, LG, Samsung and Hisense. Roku is not among them, and no update period was found on its own pages. In the US there is no legal minimum period for firmware or spare parts like the EU's, so the score is lower than for EU-registered sets with no promise.

privacy.note: Roku's US privacy policy says the Smart TV Experience lets owners enable automatic content recognition to collect what they watch, and that even with it switched off Roku still receives information about interactions and streaming on the device through other methods. In April 2025 Michigan's Attorney General sued Roku, alleging it collected children's data without notice or parental consent, and noted that 'Unlike its competitors, Roku does not offer parents the option to create children’s profiles'. The case is an allegation, not a finding.
